title: MZ The Music Dilemma – Why I Can’t Release My Game

posts.author: Archon126
posts.body:
Hi everyone,
I'm facing a bit of a dilemma.
I've been working on an RPG Maker MZ game for over 5 years now. The project is quite advanced, with more than 20 hours of gameplay already.
Unfortunately, I’ll never be able to publish or upload the game anywhere, because I exclusively use music from other commercial games.
Why?
Well, the music that comes with RPG Maker is, in my opinion, so bad that I would never consider using it. And for me, music is
extremely
important to the mood and atmosphere of the game.
I know there are some great composers out there who create music for indie projects, but I’m already using over 100 different tracks. To replace them all, I’d probably have to hire a dedicated composer just for my game — and let’s be honest, I’m not that rich.
So yeah, that’s the dilemma.
The game will likely remain something that only I will ever play.

What kind of music are you looking for? As someone who composes and writes original music, there's always original or paid substitutes that you can use in their stead. Especially if you've been working on a game for so long, might as well try and release it~!

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
There is still a solution, though you may not like it.
1: Work a side job or extra hours at the current one and bank ALL the $$$ from it to hire a composer. That is what I did with my game.
2: Find one who has released all of their work for free (we got Aaron Korgh and Desperatemeasurez here who have done that) and use their stuff. May have to compromise a little on some songs to make it work though.

posts.author: daMooseNeo
posts.body:
LOTS of resources exist for material, both original compositions and performances of public domain compositions, that can be affordably licensed. Virtually every game maker platform with a marketplace has a variety of packages ready to use for all sorts of genres, that can be purchased for $5-50, tracks or whole sets and packs.
You may have your heart set on a specific composition from a specific game but...even creatively, that's kinda cheap and cheating. Like, I frequently have tracks lodged in my head when devising certain scenes for writing, but if it came down to it seeing the light of day or not, I'd work to find something that fit the bill and, if not wholly original and unique to me, served its role well and allowed me to share with others.
Check out the major stock media companies out there, check out internet composers, look for public domain works, royalty-free works, and Creative Commons licensed works that fit your bill.
Me? I'm gearing up for that portion of my project and I have a band picked out on one of the major stock media sites and I've tapped a local friend who's a professional musician to do some additional custom work.

posts.author: Roocifer
posts.body:
I agree, music can 100% make a game in my own personal opinion. I am deeply connected to video games and franchises because of the music. Ocarina of Time alone has dominated my playlists for decades with original, revamped, remixed, and orchestral covers from both official and fan made projects. Bolero of Fire alone has 20 different versions in my rotation lol. If I cant connect to the music of the game, I usually don't connect with the game either. Partly why I am so distant to BotW/TotK...lack of music hurt but there were some good bops (Molduga theme).
There are PLENTY of free to use music out there, on Ichi.io and the links posted above. Fiverr is also a good place to get composers, but the price can range. I was looking at one that did 16-bit songs in FF style for about $15 a song but the better the package (went up to $85) the more options, like revisions, commercial usages, length, etc.
I hope you can find the solution to your music problem that wont get you in trouble. 5 years of work is too much to toss so I hope you can get what you need at the price point you desire + what's fair to the composer.
